title: Lombardia's Methane Gap Widens as Winter Demand Hits the National Market Harder
dek: Gasoline and diesel are easing back from their September peak across Lombardia and Italy alike, but self-service methane has pulled sharply apart — up 26% since July in Lombardia versus nearly 38% nationally.
executive_summary: As of November 7, self-service prices in Lombardia stand at €2.0091/L for Benzina, €2.246/L for Gasolio, €0.7906/L for GPL and €1.9056/L for Metano. Day over day, Benzina eased €0.0028 (-0.14%) and Gasolio €0.0055 (-0.24%), while GPL rose €0.0046 (+0.59%) and Metano climbed €0.0226 (+1.20%) — the sharpest single-day move of the four. Against the national self-service averages (€2.0137, €2.2503, €0.8105 and €2.1022 respectively), Lombardia's Benzina and Gasolio are both within half a cent of the national figure, GPL runs 2.5% below it, and Metano runs a full 9.4% below it.

Zoom out to the sixteen tracked weeks since July 20 (W30) and a clearer pattern emerges: Benzina and Gasolio both rose into a September peak around week W39 and have since eased back, ending the period up a modest 2.0% and 3.5% respectively in Lombardia — almost exactly mirroring the national moves of +2.2% and +3.8%. GPL and Metano never had that peak-and-retreat; both have climbed steadily through autumn and accelerated hard in the past three weeks as heating-season demand sets in. The standout finding: Metano is up 26.4% in Lombardia since July but 37.5% nationally, which has pulled the region's discount to the rest of Italy from roughly 2% in July to nearly 10% today — the region's methane advantage over the national market has not just persisted, it has nearly quintupled.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Holds Steady After Its September Spike Fades
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Lombardia sits at €2.0091/L today, down €0.0028 (-0.14%) from the November 5 reading, and €0.0046 (-0.23%) below the national self-service average of €2.0137 — a half-cent regional discount that has held fairly consistently in recent readings.

Zooming out, Lombardia's weekly Benzina average rose from €1.9722 in the week of July 20 (W30) to a peak of €2.1653 in the week of September 21 (W39) — a run-up of about 9.8% — before easing back to €2.0122 by the week of November 2 (W45), a net rise of just 2.0% since July. Nationally the shape is nearly identical: €1.9756 to a W39 peak of €2.1669, then back to €2.0184 by W45, a net rise of 2.2%. Lombardia has tracked the national Benzina cycle almost tick for tick, trading at a persistent small discount throughout.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Cools From Its Late-September Peak
paragraphs: Gasolio self-service in Lombardia is €2.246/L today, down €0.0055 (-0.24%) from November 5, and €0.0043 (-0.19%) below the national self-service figure of €2.2503 — a discount in line with Benzina's.

The weekly trend shows Gasolio climbing from €2.1744 (W30, July 20) to a peak of €2.3784 (W39, September 21) — up 9.4% — before retreating to €2.2512 by W45, a net gain of just 3.5% since July. Nationally: €2.1747 to a W39 peak of €2.3736, then back to €2.2572 by W45, a net rise of 3.8%. Lombardia's diesel has eased back slightly faster than the national average off the September peak, widening a July dead heat into today's roughly half-cent discount.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL's Quiet Convergence: Lombardia Catches Up to the National Price
paragraphs: GPL self-service in Lombardia is €0.7906/L today, up €0.0046 (+0.59%) day over day, but still €0.0199 (-2.46%) below the national self-service average of €0.8105.

The multi-week trend is the real story: Lombardia's GPL rose from €0.7135 (W30) to €0.7807 (W45) — a 9.4% increase since July — while the national average rose from €0.7592 to €0.7960, just 4.8%. Lombardia's GPL traded about 6.0% below the national price back in July; that discount has shrunk to under 2% today. Lombardia is catching up to the rest of the country on GPL faster than the rest of the country is moving.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Diverges Hard: Lombardia's Discount to Italy Nearly Quintuples
paragraphs: Metano self-service in Lombardia is €1.9056/L today, up €0.0226 (+1.20%) from November 5 — the largest day-over-day move of any fuel in today's reading — and sits €0.1966 (-9.35%) below the national self-service average of €2.1022.

This is the sharpest divergence in the dataset. Lombardia's weekly Metano average rose from €1.4682 (W30) to €1.8559 (W45), up 26.4% since July. Nationally it rose from €1.4999 to €2.0623, up 37.5% — eleven points more. In July the regional gap was negligible, about 2.1% below the national figure; by early November it has widened to roughly 10.0% below. With heating-season demand pushing methane prices up everywhere, Lombardia's network appears to be absorbing that pressure noticeably more gently than the national average.

network_section.heading: 2,832 of 3,090 Registered Stations Reporting Today
paragraphs: Lombardia has 3,090 registered fuel stations as of November 7, of which 2,832 reported prices today — a reporting rate of 91.6%, essentially unchanged from 91.7% (2,828 of 3,083) two days earlier on November 5.

Nationally, 21,661 of 23,951 registered stations reported today, a 90.4% rate. Lombardia's reporting rate runs roughly a point above the national average, even though the region accounts for just under 13% of Italy's total registered stations (3,090 of 23,951) — a sign of a comparatively well-reporting regional network relative to its size.

methodology_section.heading: Built to Run Itself: How This Report Gets Made
paragraphs: This entire report — the daily data pull, the weekly trend analysis above, the choice of which region to spotlight, and even this write-up — is generated automatically every morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent. No analyst manually recalculates Lombardia's weekly GPL average or decides which region gets today's spotlight: the rotation is a deterministic, date-keyed cycle through all 20 Italian regions that self-corrects if a day is ever missed, and every comparison above is computed directly from that day's underlying price data rather than reused from a previous day's text.

The alternative — a manually maintained spreadsheet — would require someone to download Italy's MIMIT price files every morning, paste them into a workbook, recompute weekly averages by hand, and write a fresh narrative around whatever they happened to notice, a process that tends to slip on busy days and rarely scales past one or two headline numbers. This pipeline instead covers all 20 regions, all four fuels, every tracked week, every single day, with the same rigor regardless of who is watching.

pull_quote: While national Metano prices are up 37.5% since July, Lombardia's rose just 26.4% — pushing the region's methane discount to the rest of Italy from about 2% in July to nearly 10% today.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight region is Lombardia — and the most interesting number isn't today's price, it's the trend underneath it.

Since late July, methane (Metano) prices have climbed everywhere in Italy, but not at the same pace: nationally they're up 37.5%, while in Lombardia they've risen a more modest 26.4%. That's widened Lombardia's discount to the national Metano average from about 2% in July to nearly 10% today (€1.9056/L in Lombardia vs €2.1022/L nationally, as of Nov 7). Benzina and Gasolio tell a calmer story — both rose into a September peak and have since eased back to roughly 2-4% above where they started in July, in Lombardia and nationally alike.

Fuel Dashboard tracks self-service and served prices for Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano across every Italian region, province, municipality and operator/brand, updated daily from Italy's MIMIT open price feed. No manual spreadsheet, no copy-pasted numbers: just a self-updating dashboard and report, every single day.
